newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Nationalists OK political reform package.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Nationalists OK political reform package.

text.p: Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party approved a major political reform package on Monday which would significantly boost the power of the president.
Under the ruling party's plan, the president would be granted the power to appoint a premier without parliamentary approval and dissolve the parliament when necessary.
However, as a check, the parliament would have the right to to call a vote of confidence against the premier.
The president will also have the final word on a host of important decisions on policies concerning national security, defence, foreign affairs and relations across the Taiwan Strait.
The reforms, which were approved by party members during a provisional Central Committee meeting, still need final approval from the National Assembly.
The Nationalist Party, with 183 members, has a majority in the 334-seat National Assembly, which will meet on May 5 to discuss constitutional amendments.
Critics have said the party's proposal created an all-powerful head of staff and jeopardise Taiwan's hard-won democracy.
But the Nationalist Party officials argued the proposal only granted appropriate power to the elected president.
"As long as (the reforms) are not for the interests of one party or one person, we can fearlessly face our countrymen and the history," Lee said.
President Lee Teng-hui, who doubles as chairman of the Nationalist Party, won a landslide victory in the island's historic direct presidential election in March 1996.
